theme: 3 terms on how an app starts: from nothing, from memory, and back to where you stopped

terms.definition: A start of the app when it is not in memory yet, so iOS has to load everything.
terms.example: The Cold Launch takes two seconds on an old iPhone.

terms.definition: A start of the app when it is still in memory, so it opens faster.
terms.example: A Warm Launch is quick, because the app is already in memory.

terms.definition: A feature that brings the user back to the screen where they stopped.
terms.example: State Restoration opens the same note after a restart.

quizzes.question: What do you call the feature that brings the user back to the screen where they stopped?
What do you call a start when the app is still in memory, so it opens faster?
What do you call a start when the app is not in memory yet and iOS must load everything?

video.title: Cold Launch, Warm Launch & State Restoration | Day 129
video.description:
Learn to explain how an iOS app starts and returns to where the user stopped: Cold Launch, Warm Launch & State Restoration, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Cold Launch - A start of the app when it is not in memory yet, so iOS has to load everything.
Warm Launch - A start of the app when it is still in memory, so it opens faster.
State Restoration - A feature that brings the user back to the screen where they stopped.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Cold Launch, Warm Launch and State Restoration in English?

dialogue.title: Slow in the morning

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users say the app opens slowly in the morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it a Cold Launch? iOS had to load everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. After a restart, it is a Cold Launch every time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then a Warm Launch is much faster.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why is a Warm Launch faster?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The app is still in memory, so there is less to load.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can we make the Cold Launch faster?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Do less work at startup and load data later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Users also lose their note after a restart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use State Restoration. It returns them to the screen where they stopped.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that the `stateRestorationActivity` method in the code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. State Restoration uses an `NSUserActivity` that describes the note screen.
A Cold Launch loads everything from scratch.
